title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
authors: Yu-An Chen, Meng Sun, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang
abstract: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge. We give explicit non-Pauli generators for both algebras and prove that together they generate all local operators on the Hilbert space. Starting from the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ toric code, we condense the boson $e^2m^2$ and identify the semion and anti-semion algebras. We then decompose each $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit into two qubits and use a finite-depth circuit to disentangle one qubit per edge fixed by the condensation constraints. Pumping the semion ISA along the $z$ direction defines an explicit three-dimensional non-Clifford quantum cellular automaton (QCA). We show that pumping eight times is equivalent to a translation followed by a finite-depth quantum circuit with ancillary qubits. We also give an explicit finite-depth circuit relating this construction to the semion QCA previously obtained from topological quantum field theory. A similar condensation construction yields a $U(1)_4$ ISA on a square lattice. Together with the semion and earlier odd-prime ISAs, finite stacking realizes every pointed Witt class of bosonic Abelian anyon theories. Finally, we extend both constructions to all spatial dimensions $d=4k{-}2$, with one qubit or $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit on each $(2k{-}1)$-cell for the semion or $U(1)_4$ ISA, respectively.
summary: This paper develops an algebraic framework using Invertible Subalgebras (ISAs) to model chiral semion topological order, circumventing limitations of standard local Hamiltonians. By starting from the Z4 toric code, the authors construct explicit generators for the semion and anti-semion algebras on a lattice. This work yields a concrete realization of a non-Clifford Quantum Cellular Automaton and generalizes the findings to higher dimensions.
main_problem: Chiral topological order is incompatible with standard local Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, necessitating an alternative algebraic framework.
main_result: The authors construct and characterize Invertible Subalgebras (ISAs) supporting chiral semions, demonstrating that these algebras, along with their commutants, generate all local operators on the lattice.
method: The construction uses a condensation procedure starting from the Z4 toric code, followed by disentangling circuits to realize the chiral algebras on physical qubits.
model_or_system: The model is a square lattice system where the construction is based on the Z4 toric code, leading to an ISA supporting chiral semions and its anti-semion commutant on one qubit per edge.
key_observables: The local operators generated by the semion and anti-semion algebras, and the resulting three-dimensional non-Clifford Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA).
important_parameters: The spatial dimension $d=4k-2$, and the specific topological charge structure related to the semion ($s 	imes s = 1$ with topological spin $i$).
main_assumptions: The construction assumes that the two chiral algebras are mutual commutants, and the results are stated for the infinite plane or sufficiently large periodic lattices.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the construction pathway: from the parent Z4 qudit model, through boson condensation, the disentangling circuit, to the final physical qubits carrying the two chiral algebras. Figure 2 details the lattice conventions.
paper_structure: The paper details the semion ISA construction (Section 2), the local generation proof (Section 3), the derivation of the QCA via pumping (Section 4), the equivalence to TQFT results (Section 5), and generalizations to higher dimensions and U(1) ISA (Sections 6, F, G).
why_interesting: The explicit construction of non-Clifford QCA and the realization of exotic topological order using algebraic structures like ISAs provides concrete, implementable models for quantum computation beyond standard Pauli constraints.
